name: The four passive behaviours
oneLine: Doing nothing, overadaptation, agitation, and incapacitation or violence are the four observable behaviours that always signal someone is discounting.
whatYouDid: You caught Rosita's instant, cheerful "sure, I'll take it!" as overadaptation - compliance with an assumed wish, never checked against her own, or against what was actually needed.
confusion: Overadaptation looks like cooperation and gets stroked as helpfulness, which is exactly why it's the hardest of the four passive behaviours to catch.

fromBook.quote: There are four types of behavior which always indicate that the person concerned is discounting.

expand.definition: Doing nothing discounts one's own ability to act; overadaptation discounts one's own wants in favor of an assumed wish of someone else; agitation discounts the ability to act by discharging energy into purposeless repetitive activity; incapacitation or violence discounts the ability to solve a problem directly, releasing a burst of energy against self or others instead.
expand.otherFraming: The four often chain together: agitation frequently builds up energy that later discharges as incapacitation or violence, so catching the agitation early can prevent the more damaging passive behaviour that follows it.
expand.tryThisToday: Notice the next time you give an instant, enthusiastic yes to a request - pause and check whether you actually weighed it, or just adapted to what you assumed the other person wanted.
